downgrade_statement: Author and grader now share one set of weights. A blind Opus lane is a genuine non-author and a genuine second context; it is a weaker second MIND than OW-13 intended, because correlated habits are what a same-weights reviewer is least able to see. Model-family decorrelation is therefore unavailable for the rest of the campaign, so the two-lane floor must be decorrelated by the means that remain: blind briefs that differ in method and read order, no shared intermediate files, deterministic gates wherever a check can be computed, and evidence that cites source bytes rather than another lane's prose. Every completion receipt from here on records `grader_fallback` with the model id and this statement.
receipt_rule: Every completion receipt written on or after effective_from while fallback_in_force is true carries grader_fallback = {model: declared_fallback_model, statement: downgrade_statement}, the statement byte-equal to this carrier's. A close tool reads the grader model from this carrier; it never hard-codes the fallback and never accepts an unnamed model.

The two-lane floor (OW-19) is still met - two blind non-author lanes - but the passes are no longer separate lenses, and the completion receipt must say so beside the OW-25 `grader_fallback` statement.

Dan.owner_words_transcribed: for Daniel only, I approve the merged-verdict shape as the required per-book decision. Keep two independent blind lanes, each returning the postcheck, final check and grades for items 20–23 in one pass. Record that these verdicts share a reader within each lane. Preserve every acceptance criterion. The transcript audit remains OWED / NOT MET; any status or gate requiring that audit remains blocked. Report substantive findings or disagreement before adding further review. Do not repeat completed work unnecessarily. Use compact, hash-bound handoffs and save completed review batches so quota interruptions don’t require restarting. Reuse evidence only where its artifact hashes and review scope still match. Use the most efficient available model that meets the required reviewer qualifications. Don’t silently override an Opus requirement, switch providers, or use a higher-priced speed tier. This approves Daniel’s review shape only. It does not authorize a reserved close action, waive remaining gates, or establish the choice for later books.
Dan.weakness_statement: In Daniel's close the three verdicts share one reader within each lane: a reader that misses something misses it in the postcheck, the final check and the item grades alike. The two-lane floor (OW-19) is met by two blind non-author lanes, but both run on the one fallback model family (OW-25), so their agreement is one family's voice, and the three verdicts in a lane are not three lenses. The completion receipt must say so beside the OW-25 `grader_fallback` statement.

limit: This carrier says who grades.
